<p class="eyebrow">Methods appendix · Full evidence and diagnostic maps</p>

This appendix preserves the initial 672-restaurant descriptive pool and documents the later restriction to 656 restaurants inside Census New Orleans. Read the [full results](results.html) for the final top 15, reviewer-adjusted results, sensitivity analysis, and conclusions.

## Data and large-file handling

The business and review JSON streams were read in pages of 10,000 records. The complete review scan covered 6,990,280 records and retained 476,421 reviews for 2,259 New Orleans restaurant businesses. Category selection retained 672 businesses and 250,304 reviews; the independent city-boundary check produced the final 656-business, 249,002-review pool.

Only the fields needed for rating analysis were retained. Review text and voting fields were omitted, and filtered RDS files were saved so analysis could proceed without importing the raw JSON again. The filtered records are accumulated in memory before saving; this is not a fully disk-backed import.

The user reported that RStudio was unresponsive while handling the large data. Loading and verifying the smaller RDS files through a separate R process allowed work to continue without relying on the frozen session. No memory telemetry was collected, so the freeze's cause is not established. Raw JSON and local review-level RDS files are excluded from Git; the repository contains derived results and code.

## Restaurant definition and theme

A business initially qualifies if its Yelp city is exactly `New Orleans`, its state is `LA`, and its comma-separated categories contain the exact `Restaurants` token. A match to any of **Cajun/Creole, Seafood, Southern, or Soul Food** then places it in the cooking theme. Each business counts once in the union. Both historical open and closed flags remain in diagnostic summaries; the final ranking adds the historical open-status and evidence rules described in the main report.

The label-based theme connects regional cooking traditions and seafood, but is broader than an authenticity definition. For example, a restaurant with a Seafood label can offer international cuisine. The initial city label also does not exhaust every business physically inside New Orleans: businesses labeled with another city were not recovered by that initial text filter.

## Reproducibility and source files

The main packages are `jsonlite` for streamed JSON parsing, `dplyr` for grouped summaries, `ggplot2` for charts, `sf` for spatial joins and maps, `ggrepel` for readable labels, `renv` for dependency locking, and Quarto for rendered reports. Native `sf` dependencies may still require GDAL, GEOS, and PROJ on systems without suitable binaries.

The final ranking also includes a fixed-seed bootstrap stability diagnostic. It resamples eligible reviews within each restaurant for 1,000 replicates while holding reviewer baselines, restaurant eligibility, and area membership fixed. This is deliberately described as a stability analysis rather than a claim of population-level statistical inference.

## Methods defense

The primary reviewer adjustment now uses a leave-one-review-out baseline: a review is compared with the reviewer's mean score across their other reviews. This avoids using the target review to define its own reference point. The Yelp extract contains repeated `(user_id, business_id)` pairs, so the project audits those pairs and uses true leave-one-review-out arithmetic rather than assuming one review per reviewer-business pair.

The five-review reviewer threshold, 50-review restaurant minimum, 20 eligible-reviewer minimum, and ten-restaurant ward minimum remain the primary specification. These are evidence-coverage rules, not claims of statistical significance. The sensitivity output separates reviewer selection from adjustment, includes legacy in-sample baselines, closed businesses, strict core-cuisine scope, shrinkage, and lower-confidence-bound rankings.

The ranking uncertainty analysis uses 1,000 fixed-seed bootstrap replicates, resampling eligible reviews within each restaurant and reporting rank percentiles and top-15 inclusion probabilities. Ward uncertainty additionally reports restaurant-level bootstrap intervals and a max-selection permutation test. Split-half reliability compares how consistently raw and adjusted restaurant scores reproduce across random halves; if adjustment is not more reliable, that result is retained as a limitation rather than treated as evidence in its favor. An `lme4` mixed-model cross-check is optional and is explicitly marked skipped when the package is unavailable.

The broad category theme remains the headline scope, while a strict core-cuisine sensitivity excludes businesses that match only Seafood. This is important because Yelp labels are operational categories, not authenticity evidence. Area language is intentionally limited to “highest mean among rankable wards” when the permutation test does not distinguish the winner.
